question: What primary factor does the price of retail food reflect?

options.A: Total cost from farm to table
options.B: Total weight of the grocery item

explanation: Retail food prices represent the cumulative expenses incurred during production, processing, transport, and marketing. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T026#GNS227_U2_T026_h1)

question: How do sudden spikes in food prices typically affect household dietary choices?

options.A: Dietary diversity improves due to budgeting
options.B: Families switch to cheaper calorie-dense foods
options.C: Households increase purchases of fresh organic vegetables
options.D: Consumers completely stop buying processed items

explanation: High food costs force consumers to abandon expensive nutritious foods in favor of cheap, filling carbohydrates. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T026#GNS227_U2_T026_h1)

question: What is a major input cost that directly influences agricultural production budgets?
explanation: Fertilizers and quality seeds are foundational farming inputs required before any crop can be successfully grown. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T026#GNS227_U2_T026_h2)

question: Severe droughts in agricultural regions lead to higher food prices because of what reason?

options.A: Farmers use more electricity for indoor lighting
options.B: Crop yields shrink and reduce overall market supply
options.C: Transportation trucks require higher quality fuel
options.D: Supermarkets increase profit margins during dry seasons

explanation: Weather shocks destroy harvests, creating a shortage of agricultural goods that naturally pushes market prices upward. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T026#GNS227_U2_T026_h2)

question: What happens to food prices when consumer demand exceeds the available supply?
explanation: Scarcity relative to high demand gives sellers the leverage to increase prices. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T026#GNS227_U2_T026_h3)

question: A massive agricultural surplus in local markets typically results in which outcome?

options.A: Sellers lower prices to clear inventory
options.C: Farmers destroy crops to maintain high costs
options.D: Consumers stop buying local food entirely

explanation: Excess supply forces vendors to reduce prices so they can sell perishable goods before spoilage occurs. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T026#GNS227_U2_T026_h3)

question: What is the primary purpose of agricultural input subsidies?

options.B: To lower production costs for farmers
options.D: To increase taxes on imported grain

explanation: Subsidies provide financial relief to farmers, making essential inputs like seeds and fertilizer more affordable. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T026#GNS227_U2_T026_h4)

question: How do import tariffs generally affect domestic food prices?

options.A: They increase prices of imported food items
options.B: They reduce costs for all grocery buyers
options.C: They eliminate fluctuations in local weather
options.D: They decrease the need for local labor

explanation: Tariffs add taxes to foreign goods, raising their final market price to protect local industries. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T026#GNS227_U2_T026_h4)

question: Poor road infrastructure contributes to high food prices primarily by causing what issue?

options.C: Lower fuel costs for delivery trucks

explanation: Bad roads slow down transit and damage perishable foods, destroying inventory and increasing shipping costs. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T026#GNS227_U2_T026_h5)

question: Why do high fuel prices lead to increased costs for retail food items?

options.A: Supermarkets use fuel to illuminate display aisles
options.B: Higher shipping expenses are passed down to buyers
options.C: Farmers stop using tractors during fuel crises
options.D: Crops require more gasoline to grow in the soil

explanation: Transporting food over long distances becomes expensive, forcing logistics providers and traders to raise prices. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T026#GNS227_U2_T026_h5)

question: What does food inflation represent in an economy?

options.A: A steady increase in general food prices
options.B: An expansion of agricultural land areas
options.C: A drop in the cost of farm machinery
options.D: An increase in the total weight of crops

explanation: Food inflation describes the upward trend in the cost of food baskets over a specific period. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T026#GNS227_U2_T026_h6)

question: What is the primary consequence of high food inflation on low-income households?

options.A: Reduced ability to buy nutrient-rich protein foods
options.B: Immediate elimination of all market purchases
options.C: Higher savings accounts in local commercial banks
options.D: Increased consumption of fresh fruits and vegetables

explanation: Inflation reduces purchasing power, forcing families to drop expensive healthy foods from their diets. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T026#GNS227_U2_T026_h6)

question: Which group is most vulnerable to minor fluctuations in food prices?
explanation: Low-income populations spend a huge portion of their limited earnings on food, making them sensitive to price changes. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T026#GNS227_U2_T026_h7)

question: Why do vulnerable populations suffer more during periods of food price instability?

options.A: They consume more imported luxury food items
options.B: They grow all their food in backyard gardens
options.C: They spend most of their income on basic meals
options.D: They have access to unlimited financial credit

explanation: Limited disposable income leaves poor families with zero financial buffer when food costs rise. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T026#GNS227_U2_T026_h7)

question: What health condition is commonly linked to diets restricted by high food prices?
explanation: Affordability limits force families to drop nutrient-rich foods, causing deficiencies and poor growth in children. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T026#GNS227_U2_T026_h8)

question: How do fluctuating food prices contribute to the double burden of malnutrition?

options.A: Government food programs provide too many calories to rural communities
options.B: Families rely on cheap, empty calories that cause both deficiencies and chronic disease risks
options.C: Households store excessive amounts of food until it spoils and causes food poisoning
options.D: Communities eat too many expensive fresh vegetables and develop allergies

explanation: Affordable calorie-dense foods lack essential nutrients while promoting unhealthy weight gain and chronic illness. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T026#GNS227_U2_T026_h8)
